claims.text: The magnetocaloric performance of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys is governed by the degree of chemical short-range order (CSRO).
Low-field hysteresis in these alloys is governed by the degree of CSRO.
CSRO sets the nucleation barrier of the martensitic ferromagnetic phase.
Moderate annealing introduces an optimal CSRO cluster size.
Optimal CSRO lowers the martensitic nucleation barrier.
Optimal CSRO broadens the magnetostructural transition.
Optimal CSRO reduces hysteresis with minimal loss of entropy change.
The initial material is an as-deposited Fe0.25Mn0.25Ni0.25Ge0.125Si0.125 thin film.
The as-deposited alloy is a random solid solution with minimal CSRO.
Annealing at 300–500 °C for 0.5–10 h under an inert atmosphere can tune CSRO.
Diffuse X-ray scattering intensity and diffuse-peak correlation length measure the degree of CSRO.
Moderate CSRO clustering provides abundant low-energy nucleation sites for the first-order magnetostructural transition.
The resulting reduction in effective nucleation barrier reduces thermal hysteresis while preserving latent heat.
CSRO clusters of approximately 3–5 nm will reduce thermal hysteresis by at least 10%, from about 3 K to no more than 2.7 K.
The hysteresis reduction associated with 3–5 nm CSRO clusters will incur less than a 5% reduction in peak entropy change.
Under-annealed material with low CSRO will show little change in hysteresis, whereas over-annealed material with excess CSRO will show increased hysteresis.
The as-deposited film has a peak entropy change of approximately 2.5 J kg^-1 K^-1 and thermal hysteresis of approximately 3 K at 0.5 T.
The predictions apply over annealing temperatures of 300–500 °C, durations of 0.5–10 h, applied fields no greater than 0.5 T, and temperature sweep rates no greater than 5 K min^-1.

contradictions.description: The stated initial composition has Ge:Si = 1:1 (12.5 at.% each), whereas the boundary specifies Ge:Si = 2:1.

The predicted response is non-monotonic, with little effect at low CSRO, an optimum at moderate CSRO, and increased hysteresis at excess CSRO, but the falsification rule requires a monotonic relationship between CSRO and hysteresis.
